findings.title: JobPolicy#is_org_admin? is not record-org-scoped; org isolation for the criteria endpoints rests entirely on the controller's current_organization.jobs.where scoping
findings.detail: JobPolicy.new(adminA, jobB).update?/#show? return true because is_org_admin? reads the caller's own current_organization_user, ignoring the record's org. The controller's exists(current_organization.jobs.where(id:)) returns 'no job found' (422) before policy runs for cross-org ids, so an attacker cannot read/regenerate another org's criteria. SPEC §9 line 474 explicitly documents org scoping via the controller lookup. Pre-existing shared-infra property; do NOT change policy/controller infra (pipeline rules 20/23).

findings.title: latest_ai_job_criteria / latest_succeeded_ai_job_criteria order by created_at with no secondary sort key
findings.classification: report-only (backend edge case; matches SPEC verbatim; no defect observed)
findings.detail: order(created_at: :desc).first has no tie-breaker, so an exact-microsecond created_at tie is not SQL-guaranteed to pick a specific row. In practice rows are milliseconds apart (double-POST test showed 3.4ms) and the query never raised or corrupted state across 20 probes. Practically unreachable; SPEC §3/§4.3 specify this ordering. Do not fix without owner direction.

findings.title: Canonical zero-criteria guard message is a triplicated inline string literal (no shared constant)
findings.classification: report-only (spec-compliant; matches existing inline-literal pattern in these interactors)
findings.detail: The 123-byte message is byte-identical across all 3 validators today (verified uniq == [canonical]) but nothing enforces equality on future edits. SPEC §6.2 specifies inline literals and the surrounding interactors use inline-literal errors throughout, so this matches convention. Latent drift risk only.
